data.name: Rifat
data.gender_notes: Rifat is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is frequently on the move, a traveler, a wanderer. The name Rifat carries the meaning “Traveler, Wanderer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Rifat usually hope their child will grow to embody traveler, wanderer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who is constantly seeking knowledge and wisdom through travel and exploration
data.etymology: Rifat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Traveler, Wanderer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rifat total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_pashto.name: رفات
in_pashto.meaning: رفات د عزت او لوړتیا معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: رفات د عربي نوم دی چې د 'رَفَثَ' څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې د عزت او لوړتیا معنی لري. دا نوم د الله عزت او لوړتیا ښیي او په قرآن کریم کې يې ذکر شوی دی. د افغان او پښتون دودیزو کې ددې نوم استعمال عام دی ځکه چې د عزت او لوړتیا نښه ده.

in_english.name: Rifat
in_english.long_meaning: Rifat is an Arabic name derived from 'rafa'tha', meaning excellence, sublimity, and dignity. It signifies Allah's sublimity and dignity and is mentioned in the Quran. Historically, it holds significance in Islamic tradition as a symbol of dignity and greatness. The name Rifat is used across various Muslim cultures, reflecting spiritual meaning and personality traits associated with loftiness and honor.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rifat holds a rich cultural significance in the Islamic world. Rifat is a name of Arabic origin and is widely used in many Muslim countries, particularly in the Middle East, South Asia, and North Africa. Historically, the Islamic civilization has been characterized by a deep sense of curiosity and exploration, with early Muslim scholars and travelers leaving their mark on the world through their discoveries and journeys. The name Rifat may evoke images of these brave explorers, constantly on the move, seeking out new knowledge, experiences, and adventures.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Rifat carries deep symbolism and meaning. Rifat can be seen as a reflection of the spiritual journey of the human soul, continually in search of deeper knowledge, wisdom, and connection with the Divine. The name is a reminder of the spiritual importance of travel, not just to physical places, but also to inner realms of the self. Furthermore, Rifat may symbolize the idea of being a servant of God, always moving forward, seeking out new opportunities to serve and please the Almighty. Ultimately, the name encapsulates the idea of being a seeker, a learner, and a firm believer in the ongoing journey towards self-improvement and spiritual enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Traveler, Wanderer" symbolizes One who is frequently on the move, a traveler, a wanderer. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Rifat serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of traveler, wanderer.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Rifat was a prominent commander under the Umayyad Caliph Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik (724-743 CE). The name Rifat carried significant weight in that era.

trends: Rifat is a common name in the Middle East and South Asia.
